deviations.justification: DMA hardware requires physical memory addresses as uint32_t. The TI TMS570 DMA controller uses 32-bit address registers. Pointer-to-integer conversion is the only way to provide hardware register addresses to the DMA peripheral.
deviations.risk_assessment: Low - Hardware addresses are well-defined, compile-time known values. No runtime address calculation errors possible.

deviations.justification: DMA buffer addresses must be provided as uint32_t to DMA hardware registers. The AXIVION comment documents this as 'Cast necessary for DMA configuration'. Buffer pointers are cast to hardware address format for DMA transfer setup.
deviations.risk_assessment: Low - Buffers are properly aligned and sized. DMA transfers are verified by hardware.

deviations.justification: SPI DMA configuration requires buffer addresses as uint32_t for DMA hardware. Same justification as I2C DMA - hardware interface requirement.
deviations.risk_assessment: Low - Same pattern as I2C, hardware addresses verified at compile time.

deviations.justification: RTC driver requires standard time conversion functions (mktime, localtime) for converting between RTC hardware format and epoch time. The AXIVION comment states 'Time implementation is suitable for the application'. No alternative exists for portable time calculations.
deviations.risk_assessment: Low - Time functions are used in controlled context with known input ranges. No external time zone or DST complications.

deviations.justification: Pragma SET_DATA_SECTION required to place I2C buffers in shared RAM section for DMA compatibility with cache enabled. TI compiler-specific pragma necessary for correct hardware operation. AXIVION comment documents this requirement.
deviations.risk_assessment: Low - Pragma is platform-specific but required for correct DMA operation. Well-tested pattern in TI ecosystem.

deviations.justification: Redundant expressions in SPI speed configuration macros are intentionally kept for code readability. The AXIVION comment states 'Redundant expressions are kept to enhance code readability'. The macros compute SPI prescaler values and the explicit expressions document the calculation.
deviations.risk_assessment: None - Redundant expressions do not affect runtime behavior, only compile-time constants.

quality_gate.notes: All violations have documented deviations with appropriate justifications. Hardware interface requirements necessitate pointer-to-integer conversions for DMA.

module_specific_notes.dma: DMA driver initializes hardware channels for SPI and I2C. Pointer-to-integer conversions required for hardware address configuration.
module_specific_notes.i2c: I2C driver supports polling and DMA modes. DMA buffer addresses require casting to uint32_t for hardware registers.
module_specific_notes.spi: SPI driver supports multiple interfaces with hardware/software chip select. DMA transfers use hardware address casting.
module_specific_notes.rtc: RTC driver interfaces with NXP PCF2131 over I2C. Uses standard time.h for epoch conversions.
module_specific_notes.fram: FRAM driver uses SPI for non-volatile storage. No MISRA deviations required.
module_specific_notes.adc: ADC driver uses state machine for conversion control. Clean MISRA compliance.
module_specific_notes.pex: Port expander driver uses I2C DMA. No additional deviations beyond I2C requirements.
module_specific_notes.sps: Smart power switch driver uses SPI. Clean MISRA compliance with proper state machine implementation.
